subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should strict web_fetch DNS validation allow mixed DNS result sets when at least one resolved address is public, provided blocked addresses are removed before creating the pinned dispatcher?
rationale: The code fix is small, but it changes the outbound SSRF security boundary and the existing strict-mode default, so maintainer/security intent is needed before automation should alter it.

options.title: Approve filtered-address default
options.body: Allow strict mode to proceed with only non-blocked resolved addresses, keep all-blocked sets rejected, and require focused SSRF pinning regression tests.

options.title: Keep fail-any-blocked default
options.body: Preserve the current conservative DNS policy and document useTrustedEnvProxy or explicit fake-IP/private-network opt-ins as the supported workaround.

options.title: Add a new explicit opt-in
options.body: Introduce a default-off mixed-DNS tolerance setting instead of changing strict mode for every existing web_fetch user.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered-address default
recommendation.body: Allow strict mode to proceed with only non-blocked resolved addresses, keep all-blocked sets rejected, and require focused SSRF pinning regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent history across SSRF pinned-DNS behavior, related security hardening, and maintainer policy decisions in this area.
